rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=30, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=1, outer_wall_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=iter-3 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB vs iter-1 (return to img_n_bf=1 baseline; iter-2 img_n_bf=3 was hr=0 SSIM0.9560, marginally WORSE than iter-1 0.9567 -> DEPTH compounds over-smoothing, exhausted). PRIOR: iter-1 (n_iter=120) hr=0 SSIM0.9567 PSNR38.44 recon_rmse 9.80e-4 > baseline 9.65e-4. KNOB: per-scene optimization steps n_iter 120->30 (EARLY-STOP the per-image N2I fit). HYPOTHESIS: the N2I split-MSE target is the noisy 64-view half FBP, so MORE steps pull the recon further BELOW the clean 128-view FBP (over-smooth). With the warm-start init + only 30 per-scene steps the recon stays CLOSER to the raw FBP, so recon_rmse should APPROACH baseline_rmse from above -- if hr ticks off 0, the ceiling is partly a CONVERGENCE artifact and there is an early-stop sweet spot (next: n_iter 10, 60); if hr stays 0, the N2I MSE floor is structural even at the warm-start-dominated regime. FAILURE watched: too few steps -> recon = warm-start-generic-BF (may be WORSE than a good FBP if the generic sigma over-blurs). BUDGET: n_iter 120->30 is ~4x FEWER inner steps -> expect ~350-450s, well under wall (iter-1 depth1/n_iter120 = 1200s). ONE knob: n_iter 120->30.
